evidence: Liv. 3.20.4 (Lewis & Short: “to reason captiously, to use sophisms, to quibble”)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short gives it first as to jest and mock (cum ipsō etiam cavillor ac jocor, Cic. Att. 2.1.5), then to quibble.

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 324.
